verdict.rationale: Gitea is a free, MIT-licensed self-hosted Git service. It deploys as a single binary or an official container image across many OSes and architectures, and supports several databases. Static settings live in app.ini and dynamic settings in the admin panel, and community users describe painless installs and simple binary-swap upgrades. Missing for 10: first-party upgrade and backup/restore documentation (backup is only raised as an open community question), and downgrade or rollback support (migrations reportedly go up but not down).

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can install, configure, upgrade, and maintain my own instance on my infrastructure

citations.quote: Free, self-hosted Git service under the MIT license. Full control, unlimited users and repositories.
or use container (docker/podman/etc) to deploy on your own server with the official image.
For static config options, you can edit your app.ini file and restart the instance.
Each upgrade is super simple: stop the service, replace the single binary, start it.
